passage:
Subject: Not sure when it changed
Dear Ganga,
Nobody in my team has ever told me to answer messages at night. That is the strange part. But when the lead replies at 11:30 p.m., I find my phone in my hand within a minute. Last Saturday I answered four threads before breakfast, and a small voice said, they are all awake, do not be the one who is not. Sundays now start with a knot. I used to build small clocks from scrap on weekends; that box has been shut since March and I cannot even remember why I liked it. This week I told my lead I would reply by ten in the morning on weekends, and to my surprise the answer was just "ok". I do not know if that helps yet. How did you cope at your old firm?
Santosh

qa.q: When does the lead reply at night?
What does Santosh feel on Sundays, and why?
qa.a: A knot of dread, because the week's messages and the unspoken expectation to answer them come back.

qa.q: What did Santosh try, and what could come next?
qa.a: Santosh told the lead about replying by ten on weekends; a next step could be protecting one evening and talking further with the lead.

qa.q: How might Ganga read this email?
qa.a: With sympathy, since Santosh asks how Ganga coped at an old firm, which suggests Ganga may have seen this kind of culture before.

grounding: Illustrates an employee who slowly loses rest and interest because of unspoken expectations to reply at night and on weekends.

passage: Varun, listen, you know me, Vaibhav, I never complain about work. It is not like my boss ever said "reply at midnight". It is the little stuff. Someone posts "anyone free?" on the team chat at nine on Saturday night, and three thumbs-up land within two minutes. Then it is mine to answer, or I am the one who did not. Last month I caught myself checking the chat at my cousin's engagement, out in the corridor. My sleep has gone thin, and the dashboards I used to enjoy building? I open them and feel nothing. Yesterday I realised I had not been to the badminton court in two months. I do not know how it got here, and no single day did it. Do you think it is me being soft, or is this how it starts?

qa.q: What lands within two minutes after "anyone free?" is posted?
qa.a: Three thumbs-up land within two minutes.

qa.q: What is Vaibhav worried about at the end?
qa.a: Vaibhav worries whether this is personal softness or a pressure that builds up slowly, and feels drained and uninterested.

qa.q: What small first step could Vaibhav take?
qa.a: Ask the team lead how urgent late weekend messages really are, or set a quiet evening, and go back to the badminton court.

qa.q: How might Varun respond to being asked whether Vaibhav is being soft?
qa.a: Varun might reassure Vaibhav that slow exhaustion is common and not softness, and encourage a talk with a manager.

grounding: Illustrates an employee whose rest and interest erode through unspoken late-night and weekend expectations, not one order.
